Burnham continues by saying that “Ukraine has been Europe’s protector, not a drain on our security, but the frontline of keeping Europe safe.”

title.en: Access to Zambian courts prevented as election petition deadline looms
title.zh: 阻止进入赞比亚法院，选举请愿截止日期临近

summary.en: Preparations for President Hakainde Hichilema's second inauguration appear to be continuing. Court premises in the Zambian capital, Lusaka, and elsewhere have been shut as the deadline for filing a petition against the outcome of the recent presidential election approaches.
summary.zh: 赞比亚总统哈凯恩德·希奇莱马的第二次就职典礼准备工作似乎仍在进行。随着针对近期总统选举结果提交请愿书的截止日期临近，赞比亚首都卢萨卡及其他地区的法院已被关闭。

body.en:
Court premises in the Zambian capital, Lusaka, and elsewhere have been shut as the deadline for filing a petition against the outcome of the recent presidential election approaches.

An unusual police presence has been reported at some courts, which have been taped off to prevent access.

Opposition candidate Brian Mundubile said he would challenge the election result, citing irregularities, after coming second with a 38% share of the vote. Incumbent Hakainde Hichilema won a second term with 60%.

Mundubile is in hiding over alleged threats made against him, amid a post-election period marked by controversy, including the shooting dead of an opposition figure and the arrest of others.

Monday is the last day on which petition against the presidential election result can be filed. Such a petition could potentially affect the inauguration of Hichilema, which is scheduled for 1 September.

One lawyer told the BBC that three armed men approached his vehicle, identified themselves, and instructed him to leave the area.

The courts that have been sealed off include the High Court in Lusaka, the Supreme Court, which also houses the Constitutional Court, and several local courts.

It is unclear when the premises will reopen. The BBC has contacted the Zambian police and the judiciary for comment.

Local media cite a directive by a judiciary administrative official telling all staff not to report to work following the closure of courts for "security reasons".

The memo, which has also been shared online by some opposition figures, does not give details of the security situation.

Some commentators have raised concerns over the closure while questioning the independence of the judiciary.

A prominent voice for the opposition, Emmanuel Mwamba, alleged the action was aimed at preventing Mundubile from filing his presidential election petition.

The Law Association of Zambia (LAZ) said it was concerned by the closure of the courts and the presence of heavily armed military personnel around court premises in Lusaka.

It said there was no formal public explanation for the closure nor its expected duration.

Referring to the "unsigned memorandum" from the judiciary addressing staff, it said no further official information had been provided to lawyers and the public.

It said the timing was "particularly significant in the present electoral context", citing a "seven-day period" in which a person may "petition the Constitutional Court to nullify the election of a President-elect".

Despite the court closure, preparations for Hichilema's inauguration appear to be continuing.

title.en: Iran faces 'greatest financial offensive ever', says US treasury secretary
title.zh: 美国财政部长称，伊朗面临“史上最大规模金融攻势”

summary.en: Scott Bessent says the US will sever all economic ties with the country and that any nation partnering with Iran financially will also be isolated.
summary.zh: 斯科特·贝森特表示，美国将切断与伊朗的所有经济联系，任何与伊朗进行金融合作的国家也将被孤立。

body.en:
The US treasury secretary has threated Iran with "the single greatest financial offensive ever", claiming the US-Israel war with Iran was "entering its endgame".

Scott Bessent said the US would sever all economic ties with the country in "an economic D-Day" and that any nation partnering with Iran financially would also be isolated.

Bessent's threat to the Iranian regime follows several U-turns and extended deadlines from US President Donald Trump's administration on previous threats.

Iran dismissed Bessent's comments and said it would shut down all oil exports from the region "if the war continues", according to news agency Reuters.

The Iranian regime has also issued a new warning to shipping not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission, the agency reported.

One fifth of the world's oil and gas usually passes through strait, a waterway south of Iran, but the flow has been effectively blocked by the country since the conflict began at the end of February.

Bessent made the comments in an opinion piece for the Financial Times , external . He did not detail what the economic pressure on Iran would involve, but he is expected to do so in a press conference in the US at 13:00 local time (18:00 BST) on Monday.

"The world should understand that our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains the tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," he wrote in the piece.

The US has made several threats to Iran over the course of its war with the country, including Trump saying in April that "a whole civilisation will die tonight" unless Iran agreed a deal to end the war and unblock the Strait of Hormuz.

The US eventually climbed down from that position after mediator Pakistan intervened and called for more diplomacy.

The economic impact of the Iran war is being felt in the US and across the world. Higher oil prices have fuelled concerns over the cost of living, with petrol and diesel prices much higher than they were a year ago.

In the US, gasoline prices have surpassed $4 a gallon and affordability is among the top concerns of American voters ahead of the mid-term elections in November.

On Monday, a barrel of Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil prices, was $93.

Last week, Bessent announced the US government would intervene in the bond markets and buy back more government debt in a bid to boost demand for bonds and lower borrowing rates.

But the impact of the annoucenment was short-lived, with long-term borrowing costs bouncing back up a day later.

title.en: Myanmar: Why Rohingya refugees can't return

summary.en: Nine years after the Rohingya were driven from Myanmar, claims of progress on refugee returns have revived talk of repatriation.

body.en:
Nine years after the Rohingya were driven from Myanmar, claims of progress on refugee returns have revived talk of repatriation.

Myanmar's military-backed government is again talking about bringing Rohingya refugees home from refugee camps in neighboring Bangladesh. 

Earlier this month, authorities in Naypyidaw, Myanmar's capital, said they had made progress verifying Rohingya refugees in  Bangladesh for possible repatriation.

Of the 820,000 names submitted by Bangladesh, Myanmar said it had verified around 308,000 as former residents but would not repatriate them until security conditions improve in civil war-torn Rakhine State.

But analysts told DW that large-scale, safe repatriation is now arguably further out of reach than at any point since 2017. Myanmar is engulfed in civil war, the military no longer controls most of Rakhine state , and the Rohingya are denied citizenship.

In August 2017, Myanmar's military launched sweeping operations in northern Rakhine state after alleged attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) militant group on security posts.

More than 750,000 Rohingya, a long-persecuted Muslim ethnic minority in predominantly Buddhist Myanmar, fled to Bangladesh, joining hundreds of thousands displaced by earlier crackdowns.

Muslim-majority Bangladesh now hosts around 1.2 million Rohingya refugees, mostly in camps around the southern coastal district of Cox's Bazar, according to UN bodies.

Myanmar does not recognize the Rohingya as one of its 135 officially recognized ethnic groups and has long referred to them as "Bengalis," implying they are migrants from Bangladesh despite generations of Rohingya having lived in Rakhine.

UN investigators found evidence of genocidal intent by Myanmar's military, while the United States argued in 2022 that members of the military had committed genocide and crimes against humanity against the Rohingya.

A genocide case brought by the West African nation of Gambia against Myanmar remains before the International Court of Justice in The Hague.

Myanmar's 2021 coup triggered a nationwide civil war that is still raging, even after a much-criticized election earlier this year saw the formation of a civilian government, which remains dominated by officials from the military and junta .

"Safe repatriation is simply not possible," Ronan Lee, a researcher at Loughborough University and author of the 2021 book "Myanmar's Rohingya Genocide," told DW.

There is a civil war in Myanmar and the economy has collapsed, Lee said, meaning a return under present conditions would carry a high risk of the Rohingya facing violence from the military.

title.en: Sonya Massey's killer Sean Grayson dies in US prison
title.zh: 杀害索尼娅·马西的凶手肖恩·格雷森在美国监狱去世

summary.en: The former police officer, whose crime reignited the debate about US police brutality, was undergoing treatment for cancer.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Sean Grayson, the white US police officer convicted of murdering a black woman, Sonya Massey, during an incident at her home in 2024, has died in prison at age 32.

Grayson shot dead Massey, 36, during an exchange that took place after she reported a suspected intruder at her residence in Illinois. The killing reignited the debate about police brutality in the US.

Grayson said he fired because he thought Massey was about to throw a pot of boiling water on him. He was last year found guilty of second-degree murder.

The former police officer was undergoing treatment for colon cancer. His lawyer Daniel Fultz confirmed to the BBC that Grayson had died on Sunday, but did not disclose the cause.

Lawyers for Massey's family said: "Grayson's death in custody from cancer does not bring Sonya back."

"We wish his family prayers of peace, as we do for all who grieve a loved one. Sonya's family knows that pain all too well and will grieve her loss the rest of their days," the lawyers said, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

Protests took place across the US in the aftermath of Massey's death, and then-President Joe Biden declared that the late woman "should be alive today".

The incident took place in the early hours over Independence Day weekend in July 2024. Massey called police to her home in Springfield, 200 miles (320km) south of Chicago, to report that she believed someone had broken in to her property.

The shooting happened after an exchange of words about a pot on Massey's stove. Massey and Grayson appeared to laugh over her pot of "steaming hot water", before Massey twice said: "I rebuke you in the name of Jesus."

"You better [expletive] not or I swear to God I'll [expletive] shoot you in your [expletive] face," Grayson said. He then drew his pistol as he shouted for her to drop the pot.

"OK, I'm sorry," Massey was heard saying before she ducked. Grayson fired three shots, striking her in the face.

Grayson, who was subsequently sacked from his job, was charged with first-degree murder, but the jury was allowed to convict him of the lesser charge of second-degree murder.

He was sentenced to 20 years in prison. In recent months, he applied for release on medical grounds, but was unsuccessful. He had been diagnosed with cancer in 2023.

title.en: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
title.zh: 科学家在头骨骨髓中发现新的“免疫中心”

summary.en: In mouse skull marrow, 'immune hubs' that actively defend the brain have been discovered. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

body.en:
In mouse skull marrow, 'immune hubs' that actively defend the brain have been discovered. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

The skull has traditionally been regarded largely as armor for the brain. New research from the United States  suggests it may have another role: proactively helping to defend what lies beneath it.

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis identified previously unknown immune "security stations" in the bone marrow of mouse skulls.

The lymph node-like structures responded to brain tumors before more distant lymph nodes in the neck did. When researchers disrupted the structures in mice with glioblastoma, an aggressive brain cancer , the tumors grew faster and the animals died sooner.

"The skull should no longer be viewed simply as a protective shell around the brain," senior study author Jonathan Kipnis told DW.

"It contains specialized immune environments that appear capable of responding locally to changes within the brain."

The discovery, published in the journal "Nature," comes with an important caveat: The researchers have so far only demonstrated how the structures function in mice, not humans.

Kipnis cautioned that the human evidence remains preliminary: "We found similar immune cells in human skull marrow, suggesting that related structures may exist, but we have not yet demonstrated that they are organized or function in the same way as those in mice," he said.

For much of the 20th century, the brain was described as "immune privileged" — unusually protected from immune activity because inflammation that is useful elsewhere can damage delicate brain tissue.

The blood-brain barrier, which tightly controls what can pass from the bloodstream into brain tissue, reinforced the idea that the brain was largely isolated from the body's conventional immune system.

Researchers now know that the brain communicates continuously with the immune system, particularly through tissues surrounding the brain. 

Kipnis' lab helped drive that rethink in previous work, first by identifying lymphatic vessels in the membranes surrounding the brain and later by showing tiny channels connecting those membranes to the skull's bone marrow.

"The traditional concept of immune privilege has already changed substantially," Kipnis said. "Our findings add another layer by showing that specialized immune structures exist within the skull bone marrow, immediately adjacent to the brain."

The researchers tracked proteins moving from mouse brains through microscopic skull channels and into the bone marrow.

body.en:
More than four years after Russia launched the full-scale invasion that has devastated Ukraine and claimed hundreds of thousands of lives, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is facing a new political challenge: whether to hold elections during wartime.

The issue emerged last week after former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov , who was recently dismissed from his role, called for Zelenskyy to find a way to hold elections while fighting was ongoing.

The move was seen as the biggest challenge to Zelenskyy's leadership since the invasion began in February 2022, with Zelenskyy rebuffing calls for a wartime election.

"Elections right now are a tsunami for the state, which will split Ukraine," he said on Sunday, local time.

"That's why my strategy is to steer the country toward an ending of the war and to preserve an independent and sovereign state."

National elections have been suspended since the invasion began and polling shows most Ukrainians support delaying a vote until the fighting ends.

Zelenskyy won Ukraine's 2019 presidential election in a landslide and would have ordinarily served a five-year term.

After Russia launched its full-scale invasion, Ukraine introduced martial law, which suspends some civil liberties, including national elections.

Zelenskyy's presidential term expired in 2024, but he remained in office as Ukraine's constitutional and legal system provides for continuity of government during martial law. The country's parliament has also continued operating.

Fighting continues along a front line stretching more than 1,200km, while Ukrainian cities, including the capital Kyiv, remain under regular bombardment from Russian drones and missiles.

An election would potentially require millions of Ukrainians to travel to polling stations, creating security risks and raising concerns about how voting could be conducted safely.

Political parties would also need to campaign while the country remained under attack, while authorities would have to find a way for hundreds of thousands of soldiers serving on the front line to vote.

As of the end of June, more than 4.4 million Ukrainians had temporary protection status in the European Union, meaning Ukraine would have to organise hundreds of polling stations across Europe.

Nearly four million Ukrainians have also been internally displaced, making voter registration more difficult and potentially diverting resources from the war effort.

Then there are those living under Russian occupation unable to vote. Ukrainian officials estimated that, as of 2024, around 4.5 million adult Ukrainians remained in Russian-occupied territory.

title.zh: “无法回避的辩论”：太平洋国家成为深海采矿的下一个前沿

summary.en: A new report warns that commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin as early as 2027, driven by increasing rivalry between the United States and China for critical minerals. Pacific nations are reportedly split between the promise of economic benefits and the risk of irreversible damage to the environment...

body.en:
Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin in months without policy guardrails due to increasing rivalry between the United States and China over critical minerals, a new report warns.

Analysis by the Lowy Institute has found mining could start as early as 2027, with the floor of the Pacific Ocean holding vast quantities of prized resources.

The contest between the world's two biggest economies is being driven by demand created by batteries, weapons systems, and power grids.

The region's nations are split between the promise of economic spoils and the risk of irreversible damage to the ecosystem, fisheries, food security, livelihoods and culture, according to the research.

It argues the absence of an international governance framework for commercial deep-sea mining leaves Pacific states negotiating without internationally agreed protections.

This also leaves them dependent on individual agreements drafted by companies seeking to mine their ocean floor.

"For the Pacific Island nations caught in the middle of this great power battle for critical mineral supremacy, the economic proposition is difficult to refuse," the Lowy Institute's Connor Graham writes.

"The problem is not that Pacific nations disagree, it is that they are being forced to negotiate individually against parties with vastly more resources, information, and legal capacity, and that the international framework designed to protect them has stalled."

Graham said while Australia was yet to take a clear position on deep-sea mining in the Pacific, it has the standing, relationships, and institutional presence to make an impact.

This includes its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and as a long-standing ally of the US.

"A commitment to standards that have not been written as a condition for activity that is about to begin is less of a policy, and more of an abstention," he said.

Countries including Australia have started to enter into deals for critical minerals, which are crucial for a number for emerging technologies.

The federal government has announced a $1.2 billion critical minerals strategic reserve to secure the supply of key minerals deemed crucial for Australia's economy and national security.

body.en:
Authorities in China have launched an investigation into reports of formaldehyde being used to preserve the freshness of cabbages for human consumption.

Officials in the north-eastern Hebei province confirmed that they had verified footage showing individuals dipping cabbages in a solution before loading them onto trucks for transportation.

An environmental blogger first released the footage last week. Using formaldehyde, a colourless chemical used for preserving biological specimens that is known to cause cancer, for keeping food fresh is strictly prohibited in China.

China is the world's largest producer of cabbages, most of which are exported to neighbouring countries in Asia.

Police have taken legal action against the individuals involved, according to state media.

Officials are now moving swiftly to prevent panic and restore confidence by carrying out spot checks on markets across the country.

Chinese state media says investigators will also establish how widespread the practice is and take measures to trace affected vegetables.

Local authorities in Kangbao county said in a statement issued on Saturday: "Any illegal or non-compliant practices discovered will be dealt with strictly in accordance with the law to ensure the safety of the vegetable supply."

Xinfadi market in Beijing, one of the major sources of fresh produce in the capital, issued a statement saying that it had investigated the source of its cabbages, adding that none of the affected vegetables had entered its market.

An editorial in the People's Daily wrote: "The wholesalers focused solely on their immediate economic interests while completely disregarding the lives and health of consumers. [They] crossed a legal red line and breached the moral bottom line."

China produces well over 30 million tonnes of cabbages each year, nearly half of the world's annual total. Vietnam, South Korea and Russia are among the largest export destinations for the vegetable.

Exposure to relatively high quantities of formaldehyde in some workplaces has been linked to some types of cancer in humans, but the effect of exposure to small amounts is less clear, according to the American Cancer Society.
body.zh: 中国当局已对有关使用甲醛来保鲜供人类食用的卷心菜的报道展开调查。 河北省东北部的官员证实，他们已经核实了一段视频，显示人们将卷心菜浸入溶液中，然后装上卡车进行运输。 一位环保博主上周首次发布了这段视频。中国严格禁止使用甲醛（一种用于保存生物样本的无色化学物质，已知会致癌）来保鲜食物。 中国是世界上最大的卷心菜生产国，大部分出口到亚洲邻国。 据官方媒体报道，警方已对涉案人员采取法律行动。 官员们现在正在迅速采取行动，通过对全国市场进行抽查来防止恐慌并恢复信心。 中国官方媒体称，调查人员还将确定这种做法的普遍程度，并采取措施追踪受影响的蔬菜。 康保县当地政府在周六发布的一份声明中表示：“对发现的违法违规行为，将依法严肃处理，确保蔬菜供应安全。” 北京新发地市场是首都生鲜农产品的主要来源之一，该市场发表声明称，已对大白菜的来源进行调查，并补充说，受影响的蔬菜尚未进入该市场。 《人民日报》的一篇社论写道：“批发商只顾眼前的经济利益，完全不顾消费者的生命健康。他们跨越了法律红线，突破了道德底线。” 中国每年生产超过3000万吨的卷心菜，几乎占世界年产量的一半。越南、韩国和俄罗斯是蔬菜最大的出口目的地之一。 据美国癌​​症协会称，在某些工作场所接触相对较高含量的甲醛与人类某些类型的癌症有关，但接触少量甲醛的影响尚不清楚。

reflection.en: The news of formaldehyde being used to preserve cabbages in Hebei province is a stark reminder of how easily trust can be broken in commerce. Yahweh's word reminds us that "a false balance is an abomination to Yahweh, but a just weight is his delight," emphasizing the importance of integrity and honesty in all dealings. This incident underscores the need...
reflection.zh: 河北省使用甲醛保鲜白菜的消息，严峻地提醒我们商业中信任是多么容易被破坏。雅伟的话语提醒我们：“诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶，公平的法码为他所喜悦”，强调了在所有交易中诚信的重要性。这一事件凸显了以公众福祉为先，而非追求欺骗性利益的道德实践的必要性。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: Nearly three million Teslas recalled in China over hidden door handles
title.zh: 近三百万辆特斯拉因隐藏式门把手在中国被召回

summary.en: China has issued its largest car recall, affecting over 4 million electric vehicles, including nearly three million Teslas, due to safety concerns over hidden door handles that are difficult to operate in emergencies. Chinese carmakers XPeng, Xiaomi, and Geely are also included in the recall.
summary.zh: 中国发布了有史以来最大规模的汽车召回，涉及超过400万辆电动汽车，其中包括近300万辆特斯拉，原因是隐藏式门把手存在安全隐患，在紧急情况下难以操作。小鹏、小米和吉利等中国汽车品牌也在此次召回之列。

body.en:
Minimalistic door handles became a signature feature of electric vehicles (EVs), but the controversial designs are now at the centre of China's biggest car recall, affecting more than 4 million vehicles.

The recall, which includes 2.98 million Chinese-made Teslas, follows safety concerns that the hidden door handles are difficult to locate and open in emergency situations.

Other brands affected by the recall include Chinese carmakers XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely.

The recalled vehicles will have a warning label stuck on the interior door and receive a software update to automatically lower the windows in a crash.

The designs have come under scrutiny after two fatal crashes in China involving Xiaomi EVs, in which power failures were suspected to have prevented doors from being opened.

Tesla said in a statement on Friday that it was recalling some of its Model 3, Y, S and X vehicles due to door handles that are "difficult to identify and operate because their colour is similar to the interior trim".

"In extreme situations such as a severe collision causing the vehicle's low-voltage system to fail, this could hinder occupants from quickly opening the doors to escape and impede rescue efforts by those outside the vehicle, posing a safety hazard," it said.

Tesla said it would place warning labels on the recalled vehicles and issue a software update to automatically lower a vehicle's windows after a collision.

It is not clear if the affected firms plan to make a similar recall for the rest of the world.

The use of hidden handle designs has "snowballed" after Chinese brands were quick to copy the "sleek" look of Tesla's Model S sedan since 2014, said Tu Le, the founder of consultancy Sino Auto Insights.

The use of warning labels and a software update is more of a "band-aid" than a lasting solution for the issue, he added.

Under new rules due to take effect on 1 January 2027, cars will only be allowed to be sold in China if they have a mechanical release on both the inside and outside of their doors.

Tesla's door handles were also involved in a probe by US safety regulators after reports that they suddenly stopped working, leaving children trapped in the cars.

In July, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration suggested creating a new formal safety standard for all carmakers.

How do you feel about the sleek blended in door handles? Do you have other concerns?

body.zh: 简约的可伸缩门把手已成为电动汽车 (EV) 的标志性特征，但这一颇具争议的设计目前已成为中国最大汽车召回事件的核心，影响了超过 400 万辆汽车。 此次召回包括 298 万辆中国制造的特斯拉，出于安全考虑，隐藏式门把手在紧急情况下难以找到和打开。 受此次召回影响的其他品牌包括中国汽车制造商小鹏汽车、小米和吉利。 隐藏式门把手因亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的特斯拉而广受欢迎，其设计可以无缝地塞入汽车门板内，只有当车主接近车辆时才会向外伸出。 在中国发生两起涉及小米电动汽车的致命事故后，该设计受到了严格审查，其中怀疑是电源故障导致车门无法打开。 特斯拉在周五的一份声明中表示，由于车门把手“难以识别和操作，因为其颜色与内饰相似”，该公司正在召回部分 Model 3、Y、S 和 X 车型。 这可能会阻碍乘员或救援人员在紧急情况下快速打开车门，例如在“严重碰撞导致车辆低压系统发生故障”期间。 特斯拉表示，将在召回的车辆上贴上警告标签，并发布软件更新，以在发生碰撞后自动降低车辆车窗。 目前尚不清楚受影响的公司是否计划对世界其他地区进行类似的召回。 咨询公司Sino Auto Insights的创始人涂乐表示，自2014年以来，中国品牌迅速模仿特斯拉Model S轿车的“时尚”外观，隐藏式把手设计的使用已“滚雪球”。 他补充说，使用警告标签和软件更新更像是一种“创可贴”，而不是问题的持久解决方案。 根据将于 2027 年 1 月 1 日生效的新规定，只有车门内侧和外侧均装有机械解锁装置的汽车才允许在中国销售。 特斯拉的门把手也受到美国安全监管机构的调查，此前有报道称，特斯拉的门把手突然停止工作，导致儿童被困在车内。 7月，美国国家公路交通安全管理局建议为所有汽车制造商制定新的正式安全标准。

reflection.en: The recall of nearly three million Teslas and other electric vehicles in China over hidden door handles reminds us that innovation must always be tempered with practical wisdom. While sleek designs are appealing, the potential for these handles to hinder escape in an emergency situation underscores the need for foresight in engineering. Yahweh's wisdom...
reflection.zh: 中国召回近三百万辆特斯拉及其他电动汽车，原因是隐藏式门把手存在安全隐患，这提醒我们创新必须始终与实用智慧相结合。虽然流线型设计很吸引人，但这些门把手在紧急情况下可能妨碍逃生，这突显了工程设计中预见性的重要。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们考虑所有可能的结果，确保便利性和美观性不会损害安全和福祉。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: 'Can't abstain from this debate': Pacific nations the next frontier in deep-sea mining
title.zh: “无法回避的辩论”：太平洋国家成为深海采矿的下一个前沿

summary.en: A new report warns that commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin as early as 2027, driven by increasing rivalry between the United States and China for critical minerals. Pacific nations are reportedly split between the promise of economic benefits and the risk of irreversible damage to the environment...
summary.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国之间对关键矿产的竞争日益加剧，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能最早在2027年开始。据报道，太平洋国家在经济利益的承诺与对环境和当地生计造成不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。

body.en:
Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin in months without policy guardrails due to increasing rivalry between the United States and China over critical minerals, a new report warns.

Analysis by the Lowy Institute has found mining could start as early as 2027, with the floor of the Pacific Ocean holding vast quantities of prized resources.

The contest between the world's two biggest economies is being driven by demand created by batteries, weapons systems, and power grids.

The region's nations are split between the promise of economic spoils and the risk of irreversible damage to the ecosystem, fisheries, food security, livelihoods and culture, according to the research.

It argues the absence of an international governance framework for commercial deep-sea mining leaves Pacific states negotiating without internationally agreed protections.

This also leaves them dependent on individual agreements drafted by companies seeking to mine their ocean floor.

"For the Pacific Island nations caught in the middle of this great power battle for critical mineral supremacy, the economic proposition is difficult to refuse," the Lowy Institute's Connor Graham writes.

"The problem is not that Pacific nations disagree, it is that they are being forced to negotiate individually against parties with vastly more resources, information, and legal capacity, and that the international framework designed to protect them has stalled."

Graham said while Australia was yet to take a clear position on deep-sea mining in the Pacific, it has the standing, relationships, and institutional presence to make an impact.

This includes its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and as a long-standing ally of the US.

"A commitment to standards that have not been written as a condition for activity that is about to begin is less of a policy, and more of an abstention," he said.

Countries including Australia have started to enter into deals for critical minerals, which are crucial for a number for emerging technologies.

The federal government has announced a $1.2 billion critical minerals strategic reserve to secure the supply of key minerals deemed crucial for Australia's economy and national security.

title.en: Robot boxing, football and sprinting at World Humanoid Games
title.zh: 机器人拳击、足球和短跑亮相世界人形机器人大赛

summary.en: The second-edition of the five-day competition kicked off in Beijing, China, on Saturday.
summary.zh: 第二届为期五天的世界人形机器人大赛于周六在中国北京拉开帷幕。

body.en:
The competition, which kicked off on Saturday, will run for five days and has already included a robot running faster than Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record.

Elsewhere at the event in Beijing, a robot performed Cristiano Ronaldo's iconic 'Siuuu' celebration on the football pitch and droids took part in synchronised marching at its opening ceremony.

Robots have also been competing in events including boxing, high jump, Tai Chi and table tennis.

The BBC's China correspondent Stephen McDonell reports from the country's capital.
body.zh: 这场比赛于周六开始，将持续五天，其中已经有一个机器人跑得比尤塞恩·博尔特 (Usain Bolt) 的 1 亿短跑世界纪录还要快。 在北京的其他地方，机器人在足球场上表演了克里斯蒂亚诺·罗纳尔多标志性的“Siuuu”庆祝动作，并且机器人在开幕式上参加了同步行进。 机器人还参加了拳击、跳高、太极拳和乒乓球等项目的比赛。 英国广播公司 (BBC) 驻华记者史蒂芬·麦克唐纳 (Stephen McDonell) 从该国首都进行报道。

reflection.en: The World Humanoid Games in Beijing, featuring a robot that outran Usain Bolt's 100m record, showcase humanity's remarkable ingenuity and drive for achievement. As we marvel at these technological feats, Yahweh's word reminds us that while athletes strive for a perishable crown, there is a greater, imperishable one to be sought. This perspective encourages...
reflection.zh: 在北京举行的世界人形机器人大赛上，一台机器人跑出了比博尔特100米世界纪录更快的成绩，这展现了人类卓越的创造力和追求成就的动力。当我们惊叹于这些科技壮举时，雅伟的话语提醒我们，运动员们所争取的不过是会朽坏的冠冕，而我们当寻求的，是那永不朽坏的。这种视角鼓励我们在赞美人类创新的同时，将我们最终的盼望根植于真正永恒的事物。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.

title.en: Sam was jailed for helping Hong Kong's protesters. He came home to a city in silence
title.zh: 香港镇压异见，山姆出狱后发现城市一片寂静

summary.en: Six years after China imposed the National Security Law, Hong Kong's crackdown on dissent has spread beyond its borders.
summary.zh: 中国实施《国家安全法》六年之后，香港对异见的镇压已蔓延至境外。

body.en:
Watch Dateline’s latest episode, Hong Kong: A City Silenced, on 25 August at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand.

At 21, Sam Chan Chi-sum was preparing to leave Hong Kong to continue his studies overseas.

He'd been involved with a student activist group that collected sweets and toiletries to send to people jailed after Hong Kong’s 2019 anti-government protests.

Authorities accused the group of using the supplies to build support among prisoners and incite opposition to the government.

In September 2021, Sam was arrested under Hong Kong’s sweeping National Security Law, which had been passed a year earlier, and was convicted of "subversion with the intent of overthrowing the government".

"Prison was awful. I shared a cell with around twenty people. At its most crowded, there could be forty of us," he said.

He alleged some prison officers purposely mistreated inmates associated with the protest movement.

"I don't know whether they were acting out of personal conviction or following orders. But they certainly made life difficult for us."

Two years after his release from prison, Sam is trying to rebuild a normal life.

He had dreamt of becoming a teacher or a nurse, but his criminal record prevents him from pursuing either career.

"Since being released from prison, I feel as though I've entered a much larger cell," he said.

Instead, he is training to become a documentary filmmaker, determined, he says, to capture the transformation of Hong Kong.

"Whatever the outcome for Hong Kong, whether the future is good or bad, I want to stay here and witness the changes that lie ahead."

Sam’s story is like many other young Hongkongers whose lives have been upended by China’s crackdown on freedoms in Hong Kong, a city once known for its outspoken press, independent judiciary and political opposition.

In 1997, after more than 150 years of British rule, Hong Kong was handed back to China under the "one country, two systems" arrangement that promised Hong Kong would keep a high degree of autonomy.

Like Sam, Carmen Lau was from a generation that came of age after this handover to China: neither British, nor truly Chinese.

As a teenager, Carmen led a student movement in her secondary school against the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) attempt to introduce 'patriotism' lessons in Hong Kong schools.

Many Hongkongers feared it would promote the CCP’s version of patriotism in their city.

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

title.en: 130,000 or 230,000? The migration figures One Nation is trying to explain
title.zh: 13万还是23万？一国组织试图解释的移民数据

summary.en: Conflicting comments from One Nation figures have raised questions about the party's migration target.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce has faced questions over his party's immigration target, claiming fellow MP David Farley misspoke when he revealed their figures were "not too different" from Labor's.

The MP for Farrer told ABC's Insiders program on Sunday that One Nation's stated figure of 130,000 net overseas migration annually into Australia did not include those who enter under a Pacific labour scheme, aged-care nurses, and other in-demand skilled workers.

He conceded that those groups would add roughly 100,000 people, bringing their total to 230,000 — 5,000 fewer than the current Labor budget projections.

Party leader Pauline Hanson intervened just hours later, writing on social media that One Nation's policy is to reduce net overseas migration (NOM) to 130,000.

Speaking to Channel Seven's Sunrise program on Monday, Joyce added that Farley simply made a mistake while explaining the numbers.

"Show me a political career where people haven't made a mistake, and I'll show you a person who's not told the truth," Joyce said.

"I'm not going to throw anybody under a bus. When people are new in parliament, they can sometimes get things incorrect, and that's what happens. God knows, I've done it enough."

The debate over Australia's migration figures has intensified in recent months, with a recent Redbridge/Accent Research poll, conducted for the Australian Financial Review, indicating that voters trust One Nation and its traditionally restrictive approach to handle migration better than Labor or the Liberal Party.

However, the disjointed nature of One Nation's ongoing public discourse on the topic has prompted claims that the party is "incoherent" and "not fit to govern" from federal minister Pat Conroy.

Since its 1997 inception, cutting immigration has been seemingly a foundational pillar of One Nation policy. During her first speech to federal parliament, Hanson alleged Australia was in danger of being "swamped by Asians", that migrants never assimilated, and that multiculturalism should be abolished.

Its website currently states One Nation would "cut immigration by over 570,000 people" through "capping visas at 130,000 per year".

In a social media post on Sunday, Hanson wrote that NOM would be cut to 130,000 — a figure the party has previously clarified to SBS News . This number would be achieved by reducing international students, temporary graduate visas, and a "much more targeted" skilled migration program, Hanson said.

title.en: Rush to vaccinate little penguins against H5N1 as another seal is diagnosed

summary.en: A second seal has contracted the virus in South Australia, as Phillip Island rushes to vaccinate its iconic bird population.

body.en:
Bird flu has likely spread to a second seal, one day after the first mammal in Australia was confirmed to have contracted the virus.

Five suspected H5 bird flu cases were recorded in South Australia on Monday, including a long-nosed fur seal at The Pages Conservation Park, the state's Department of Primary Industries and Regions said in a statement on Monday morning.

The Pages — which covers two small islands between Kangaroo Island and the mainland — is a haven for the endangered Australian sea lion.

The fur seal has been tested for bird flu, with results expected in the coming days.

The first positive case of the virus in a mammal was confirmed on Sunday in a long-nosed fur seal at Beachport, 300km south of Adelaide, which authorities believed was contracted from wild birds.

Before the new case was announced, Environment Minister Murray Watt said the spread from birds to mammals was inevitable and the government was examining whether further vaccination programs were needed.

"We are likely to see mass mortalities of birds and mammals, and I know that is a very distressing thing for Australians to hear. But we also need to be realistic," he told ABC TV on Monday.

"This is what we've seen happen overseas. Australia is very fortunate that we've been the last continent on Earth to have this strain of bird flu happen. But we are likely to see those kind of events as we have overseas."

Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said the federal government was investigating whether bird flu vaccines were available for use in mammals.

"There are trials underway in North America, in California and Hawaii, and this is using a vaccine that's been developed for cattle," she told ABC radio.

"There certainly is nothing commercially available, but we do continue to look at that research."

Bird flu vaccinations have been rolled out to at-risk species, including the little penguins on Victoria's Phillip Island.

Many were corralled into pens to receive the first of two vaccinations on Sunday night.

With case numbers on the rise, authorities have stepped in to do what they can to defend the 5,000-strong colony.

The penguins' nightly ritual of returning to the same burrow, along the same path, made them ideal candidates for vaccination, Phillip Island Nature Parks reserve manager Ben Thomas said.

As a world-first in scale, the process has taken some experimentation and fine-tuning.

"We've had our teams out late into the night for a week now and learning a lot along the process," Thomas said.

title.en: SBS WorldWatch is changing. Here's what viewers need to know
title.zh: SBS WorldWatch 正在发生变化。这是观众需要了解的内容

summary.en: The multilingual news service will cease broadcasting next month and continue exclusively online.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
SBS WorldWatch will soon become a digital-only service, ending its run as a broadcast television channel.

The multilingual news service, which provides news bulletins from international broadcasters, will move entirely to SBS On Demand .

SBS says the shift will allow it to increase the number of bulletins available in most languages.

From 18 September, the channel, which provides international news in 38 languages from 49 broadcasters worldwide, will cease broadcasting and all SBS WorldWatch programming will continue on SBS On Demand.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

As the channel closes, SBS WorldWatch will expand its existing digital service over the coming weeks to include two or more daily bulletins in most languages.

This is more content than could be accommodated on a single linear channel, SBS says, allowing audiences to watch bulletins as soon as they become available rather than waiting for a scheduled broadcast.

SBS On Demand also features two 24-hour FAST channels for English-language news — Euronews and France 24 .

SBS Director of News and Current Affairs, Mandi Wicks, said SBS WorldWatch played an important role in connecting Australians with news and perspectives from around the world, in their preferred language.

"Moving to SBS On Demand gives us the opportunity to build on that service, with more international news bulletins and greater flexibility for audiences to decide when and how they watch," she said.

"We recognise this will be a change for some audiences who are accustomed to watching SBS WorldWatch on linear television. We're committed to supporting them through the transition, while continuing to evolve our services for the future."

SBS is providing multilingual information and guidance through SBS Audio language programs and on SBS WorldWatch channel 35 ahead of the change.

Further information is available here , with additional support available via the SBS Help Centre .

The SBS WorldWatch — News In-Language hub can be found on the SBS On Demand homepage , where audiences can also search for content in their preferred language.

The full SBS On Demand offering features more than 15,000 hours of local and international programming across more than 60 languages, spanning news and current affairs, documentaries, drama, world movies, entertainment, food, children’s content and sport.

This includes dedicated language collections, as well as selected English-language programs with subtitles in Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, and Vietnamese.

title.en: 'Second chance at life': Sydney woman speaks publicly after surviving shark attack
title.zh: “第二次生命机会”：悉尼女子鲨鱼袭击幸存后首次公开讲话

summary.en: Leah Stewart, 34, a Sydney mother, has spoken publicly for the first time since surviving a shark attack over two months ago, attributing her "remarkable" recovery to community support. She expressed gratitude for the "army of love, support, prayers and encouragement" that helped her "get better, not bitter."
summary.zh: 34岁的悉尼母亲莉亚·斯图尔特在两个多月前鲨鱼袭击中幸存后首次公开讲话，她将自己“显著”的康复归功于社区的支持。她对“来自世界各地的爱、支持、祈祷和鼓励大军”表示感谢，这些帮助她“变得更好，而不是心怀怨恨”。

body.en:
A Sydney mother has spoken publicly for the first time since surviving a shark attack more than two months ago, crediting community support with helping her "get better, not bitter".

In a post on her GoFundMe donation page, Leah Stewart, 34, said she still had a long way to go, but her recovery had been "remarkable".

"A huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world," she said.

"That means more to me than I can say, and I truly believe it’s played a huge role in my recovery."

Stewart was swimming between the flags close to shore when she was attacked by a great white shark at Coogee Beach on 13 June.

She was rushed to hospital in a critical condition, being induced in a coma and undergoing multiple surgeries, including the amputation of one of her arms.

The mother of one said she had been focused on her recovery and had "progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this".

"I want you to know that I feel like I’ve been given a second chance at life, and I’m not going to waste it. As I get better, I know I’ll make something of this second chance and aim to give back even more in generosity, care, and love. I will forever be grateful for everything, and everyone, I’ve been given," she said.

Stewart thanked those who had contributed to the fundraiser, which had reached more than $558,000, but it was time to turn donations off.

"What you’ve offered has given us enough to recover, to stay in our home, and to give us options for further medical treatment down the road," she said.

Sydney has experienced a spate of shark attacks this year, including three in just 48 hours in January.

On 18 January, 12-year-old Nico Antic was critically injured and later died after being attacked by a suspected bull shark while swimming off rocks in Vaucluse in Sydney Harbour.

The following day, Andre de Ruyter, 27, was attacked while surfing near Manly, suffering extreme blood loss and undergoing surgery to have one of his legs amputated.

An 11-year-old boy's surfboard was also bitten at Dee Why Beach on the same day, but the young surfer escaped injury.

After Stewart was attacked in June, NSW Premier Chris Minns said his government would invest an extra $34 million in drone coverage across NSW beaches.

Should you invest in shares, or property? Is university still worth it, or should you start your own business? With the path to financial security becoming less clear, Insight asks how aspirational people are getting ahead, and whether Australia is a good country to build wealth. Watch Insight episode Gettin' Rich at 8.30PM Tuesday 25 August on SBS or SBS On Demand.

Enosh Tampoe, 23, and his family migrated from Sri Lanka 16 years ago and have been living in the same rental property since then.

The Sydney mortgage and finance adviser says that as an immigrant family "starting from scratch", he felt financially behind his friends at times growing up.

"There were situations where I did feel like [I was] potentially behind — just because at the end of the day, there is that intergenerational wealth ...You'll notice obviously, they have their own houses; they have nice cars ..." he told Insight.

"Having that support from parents — whether it's in the form of getting money or continuing to live at home rent-free and all that stuff — definitely helps."

Feeling he couldn't rely on the "whole natural pathway of doing well in school, getting through uni and [getting] a big boy job" to build wealth, he took a hard approach to saving at an early age and bought a Sydney apartment two years ago.

Now, he's giving himself 10 years to save a $600,000 deposit for a $3 million Sydney home where his whole family can live.

"My end goal is … that great Australian dream: owning my own home, building my family and raising them in a nice neighbourhood," he said.

To reach his goal faster, he lives with his parents and rents out his apartment — taking advantage of the tax benefits of negative gearing to build equity.

Negative gearing refers to a situation where the ongoing costs of an investment exceed the rental income received, and the overall loss can then be claimed as a tax deduction.

But as of 1 July 2027, the federal government will restrict the tax benefits of negative gearing to new residential builds.

Enosh says this new law has reduced his borrowing capacity by "around 20 per cent", putting his plans to buy a second investment property this year on hold.

"If I were to purchase a second investment property, I'm not getting that benefit towards my salary or wage, that tax benefit."

title.en: 'Link workers' help fight elderly loneliness
title.zh: “链接工作者”帮助对抗老年人的孤独感

summary.en: One of Ben Wong's clients is an elderly man who shunned others after his dog died. "At his home, there were only some instant noodles and alcohol," Wong spoke about his client's sense of isolation. The volunteer "link worker" noted it took him some time to gradually get the man...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自香港栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: One of Ben Wong's clients is an elderly man who shunned others after his dog died. "At his home, there were only some instant noodles and alcohol," Wong spoke about his client's sense of isolation. The volunteer "link worker" noted it took him some time to gradually get the man to open up, revealing more about himself and his beloved four-legged companion. Among the activities planned was a funeral to allow his client to bid farewell to his dog. Accompanied by Wong, he also met with other dog owners and went to parks and markets. "We also took the elderly man to the district elderly community centre, and he even did rehearsals for the centre's Christmas party," Wong said. "He also started to do hotpots with other senior residents and said hi to his friends." Wong, who's in his fifties and an accountant by profession, is training to become a volunteer "link worker" to help elderly people fight their loneliness by linking them with the appropriate activity resources. He is among a batch of 60 "link workers" under a programme that offers "social prescriptions" for some 300 senior citizens in New Territories East, including Tin Shui Wai, Tun Mun and Yuen Long. "Social Prescribing Lab 2.0", to be launched next year, was organised by Make A Difference Institute, the city's first community-initiative public services innovation lab, to provide personalised services for those in need. The group said Hong Kong is grappling with a "loneliness epidemic", with one in five people reporting they feel lonely. That's higher than the global average of 16 percent. Roughly 520,000 Hongkongers also noted that they are "self-isolating", unwilling to confide in family, friends or even AI, according to surveys. "[For] many of the senior residents, actually they don't have the physical illnesses, what they really need is the 'social prescribing' to help them cope with loneliness," the institute's chairwoman Ada Wong said. Dicky Chow, assistant research director of the think tank, Our Hong Kong Foundation, highlighted the differences between social workers in general and these "social prescribing link workers". He said while social workers offer various types of services, "link workers" bring their clients to the actual social venues or help them access social resources. "'Social prescribing' is actually serving as a bridge between medical and social sectors," Chow said. "It's connecting the social sectors with the healthcare sectors, but at the same time, it is not [done] through just referrals, but more about accompanying the elderly, the patients... go through the whole journey with them. "And this is particularly helpful in solving a lot of health concerns, especially loneliness and chronic diseases, because they're actually affected by social determinants of health...
body.zh: Ben Wong 的一位客户是一位老人，在他的狗死后，他避开了其他人。 “在他的家里，只有一些方便面和酒，”黄谈到他的客户的孤立感。这位志愿者“链接工作人员”指出，他花了一些时间才逐渐让这名男子敞开心扉，透露更多关于他自己和他心爱的四足伙伴的信息。计划的活动之一是举行葬礼，让他的客户告别他的狗。在黄的陪同下，他还与其他狗主人会面，并去了公园和市场。黄说：“我们还带老人到区长者社区中心，他甚至为中心的圣诞晚会进行排练。” “他还开始和其他老人一起做火锅，并向朋友们打招呼。”黄先生五十多岁，职业是会计师，他正在接受培训，成为一名志愿者“联络员”，通过为老年人联系适当的活动资源来帮助他们克服孤独感。他是一项计划中的60名“链接工作者”之一，该计划为天水围、屯门和元朗等新界东约300名老年人提供“社会处方”。将于明年推出的“社会处方实验室2.0”是由Make A Difference Institute组织的，该实验室是该市第一个社区倡议的公共服务创新实验室，旨在为有需要的人提供个性化服务。该组织表示，香港正在应对“孤独流行病”，五分之一的人表示他们感到孤独。这高于 16% 的全球平均水平。调查显示，大约 52 万香港人还表示，他们正在“自我隔离”，不愿向家人、朋友甚至人工智能倾诉。 “对于许多老年居民来说，实际上他们并没有身体疾病，他们真正需要的是‘社会处方’来帮助他们应对孤独，”该研究所的主席 Ada Wong 说。团结香港基金智囊团助理研究主任周卫健强调了一般社会工作者与这些“社会处方链接工作者”之间的差异。他说，虽然社会工作者提供各种类型的服务，但“链接工作者”将他们的客户带到实际的社交场所或帮助他们获取社会资源。 “‘社会处方’实际上是医疗和社会部门之间的桥梁，”周说。 “它正在将社会部门与医疗部门联系起来，但同时，它不仅仅是通过转介来完成的，而是更多地陪伴老年人、患者……与他们一起经历整个旅程。“这对于解决很多健康问题特别有帮助，特别是孤独和慢性病，因为它们实际上受到健康的社会决定因素的影响......

summary.zh: 这是一则来自香港栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: China’s manned space agency said on Sunday it is delaying a research moon mission that is part of Beijing’s efforts to land a crew there by 2030, less than two weeks after a rare launch failure. The Chang’e-7 lunar probe on a Long March 5 carrier rocket. Photo: CCTV screenshot. The agency said after a “comprehensive assessment” the mission, which involved sending the Chang’e-7 lunar probe on a Long March 5 carrier rocket, “does not meet launch conditions and cannot take place during the planned window this year”. The decision to delay was “based on the principle of prudence, reliability and absolute mission success,” it added, without providing further details on what conditions weren’t met or when the launch would be rescheduled. The mission — meant to search for water on the moon’s south pole — was scheduled to depart either over the weekend or Monday, according to media reports. Last week, the agency said the probe and carrier rocket had been moved to the takeoff area at Wenchang Space Launch Center in southern Hainan province. As of Wednesday, the takeoff site and equipment were in good condition, with inspections to take place and a launch “scheduled for the coming period”. The Chang’e-7 delay comes just under two weeks after media reports showed a rocket launched from the Hainan site had exploded, as crowds watched a fiery ball in the sky. The failed mission involved a Long March 7A carrier rocket, which had lifted off from the Wenchang Space Launch Site, state news agency Xinhua said at the time. China’s Long March 7A carrier rocket exploded on Monday, August 10, 2026. Photo: Supplied. An “anomaly” occurred when the rocket carrying the Zhongxing-4B communications satellite was in flight, Xinhua added. The cause of the failure was under investigation, it said. Beijing has ploughed billions of dollars into its space programme in recent years to achieve what President Xi Jinping calls the country’s “space dream”. China successfully landed a reusable rocket for the first time in July, according to its space agency, marking a major step in its space ambitions and in reducing launch costs. The country is aiming to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, a race in which the United States is also competing with its Artemis programme.

body.en: Shein will debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange on September 1, the fast-fashion retailer said on Monday, in a long-awaited listing that would value the group at close to US$27 billion. Shein app. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The online retailer plans to offer 280 million shares at a price between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50, raising up to HK$13.86 billion (US$1.7 billion), it said in a filing to the bourse. The final price will be announced on August 31, but the higher figure would value the company at around US$26.8 billion. Founded in China and now headquartered in Singapore, Shein finally won Beijing’s approval last month to make its initial public offering in Hong Kong. Plans to list in New York and London had been held back in recent years by regulatory hurdles, according to media reports. With most of its factories located in China, Shein sets itself apart from its competitors thanks to the speed of its product design and its highly efficient production and supply chain. Its vast selection of products at stunningly low prices has brought Shein into the same league as Amazon in the United States. With the funds raised from the market, Shein said it aims to finance its technological capabilities as well as boost its international presence. Growing scrutiny Shein reported a full-year net profit of US$2.06 billion in 2025 but swung to a $99 million quarterly loss as the United States scrapped an import duty exemption on small packages. The firm moved its headquarters to Singapore between 2021 and 2022, a move analysts say was intended to avoid increasing global scrutiny of Chinese firms. But it still benefits from China’s unique combination of a huge, low-cost textile manufacturing sector and a highly sophisticated e-commerce logistics network. The company ranks suppliers by their flexibility and ability to deliver urgent orders, and regularly eliminates the poorest performers, according to a 2021 Zhongtai Securities report. By the end of last year, its European customer base rose to 156 million average monthly users, making Shein one of the continent’s biggest e-commerce platforms alongside China’s AliExpress (193 million users) and Amazon (around 180 million). Shein has been scrutinised over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, though its executive chairman told AFP last year that the company has “zero tolerance” on forced labour. Activists from Mouv’Enfants, an association for the protection of children, stage a protest during the opening of Asian e-commerce giant Shein’s first physical store at the Bazar de l’Hotel de Ville (BHV) in Paris on November 5, 2025. Photo: Mouv’Enfants, via Facebook. Shein also drew criticism last year in France over the discovery of...
body.zh: 这家快时尚零售商周一表示，Shein 将于 9 月 1 日在香港证券交易所上市，这是一次期待已久的上市，该集团的估值将接近 270 亿美元。谢因应用程序。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。该在线零售商计划以 47.60 港元至 49.50 港元的价格发行 2.8 亿股股票，筹集至多 138.6 亿港元（17 亿美元）。最终价格将于 8 月 31 日公布，但较高的价格将使该公司估值约为 268 亿美元。 Shein 成立于中国，现总部位于新加坡，上个月终于获得北京方面的批准，在香港进行首次公开​​募股。据媒体报道，近年来在纽约和伦敦上市的计划因监管障碍而受阻。 Shein 的大部分工厂位于中国，凭借其产品设计速度以及高效的生产和供应链，使其在竞争对手中脱颖而出。 Shein 的产品种类繁多且价格极低，使其与美国的亚马逊处于同一水平。 Shein 表示，通过从市场筹集的资金，其目标是为其技术能力提供资金并提高其国际影响力。日益严格的审查 Shein 报告称，2025 年全年净利润为 20.6 亿美元，但由于美国取消小包装进口关税豁免，季度亏损 9,900 万美元。该公司在 2021 年至 2022 年间将总部迁至新加坡，分析师称此举是为了避免全球对中国公司日益严格的审查。但它仍然受益于中国庞大、低成本的纺织制造业和高度复杂的电子商务物流网络的独特结合。根据中泰证券 2021 年的报告，该公司根据供应商的灵活性和交付紧急订单的能力对供应商进行排名，并定期淘汰表现最差的供应商。截至去年年底，其欧洲客户群平均每月用户数增至 1.56 亿，使 Shein 成为欧洲大陆最大的电子商务平台之一，与中国的全球速卖通（1.93 亿用户）和亚马逊（约 1.8 亿用户）齐名。 Shein 因其环境足迹和侵犯人权的指控而受到审查，尽管其执行主席去年告诉法新社，该公司对强迫劳动采取“零容忍”态度。 2025 年 11 月 5 日，保护儿童协会 Mouv’Enfants 的活动人士在亚洲电子商务巨头 Shein 在巴黎 Bazar de l’Hotel de Ville (BHV) 的第一家实体店开业期间举行抗议。照片：Mouv’Enfants，来自 Facebook。去年，谢因在法国也因发现……而受到批评。

body.en: The government has awarded the first tender for a major land parcel in the Northern Metropolis. The Development Bureau announced on Monday that the site, located in the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen New Development Area, goes to HSK New Development Limited with a bid price of HK$1.03 billion. The winning consortium comprises six shareholders: China Overseas Land and Investment, China Merchants Land, China Resources Land, China Travel Service, JD.com and a subsidiary of Sino Land. The project, featuring nearly 11 hectares, is the first "large-scale land disposal" under the Northern Metropolis. Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said the consortium brings together major property developers and industry leaders from other sectors. "The six companies have joined forces and cast a vote of confidence in the Northern Metropolis through concrete action, ushering in a promising start for the diversified development model," Linn said. The winning bidder will be responsible for flattening and developing three residential sites that can yield about 3,000 flats, with an average size of 50 square metres each. It will also build a smart logistics centre on an "Enterprise and Technology Park" site, with a total floor area of 50,950 square metres. JD.com will be the anchor tenant, with operations starting within 55 months – well ahead of the 96-month minimum requirement in the tender documents. The three residential sites and one Enterprise and Technology Park site, totalling about 3.6 hectares, will be granted to the consortium on 50-year leases. The consortium estimates the entire project involves about HK$16.8 billion in investment and will create more than 6,000 jobs. It has chosen to pay the full land premium within 28 days, rather than in instalments. The government received two bids for the tender exercise which ended in July. Edited by Edmond Fong
body.zh: 政府已授予北部大都市一块主要地块的首次招标。发展局周一公布，位于洪水桥／厦村新发展区的地皮落予HSK新发展有限公司，竞投价为10.3亿港元。中标财团由六家股东组成：中国海外发展、招商局置地、华润置地、中国旅行社、京东以及信和置业的子公司。该项目占地近11公顷，是北方都市圈首个“大规模土地出让”。发展局局长伯纳黛特·林恩 (Bernadette Linn) 表示，该财团汇集了主要房地产开发商和其他行业的行业领导者。 “六家企业强强联手，以实际行动为北方都市投下了信任票，为多元化发展模式开启了良好的开局。”林恩说。中标者将负责平整和开发三块住宅用地，可建造约3,000套公寓，每块平均面积为50平方米。还将在“企业科技园”用地建设智慧物流中心，总建筑面积50,950平方米。京东将成为主要租户，并在 55 个月内开始运营——远远早于招标文件中 96 个月的最低要求。这三块住宅用地和一处企业科技园用地总计约3.6公顷，将以50年的租约授予该财团。该财团预计整个项目投资约168亿港元，将创造超过6,000个就业机会。它选择在 28 天内支付全额土地出让金，而不是分期付款。政府在七月份结束的招标活动中收到了两份标书。埃德蒙·方编辑

title.en: Reframing Homer's Sirens through gender, nature and social order

summary.en: Though they are pivotal to Homer's epic, luring Odysseus with the promise of eternal wisdom, the Greek poet barely described the mysterious Sirens. What might a better understanding of these formless, disembodied feminine creatures contribute to this timeless teaching myth?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

Though they are pivotal to Homer's epic, luring Odysseus with the promise of eternal wisdom, the Greek poet barely described the mysterious Sirens. What might a better understanding of these formless, disembodied feminine creatures contribute to this timeless teaching myth?

Han Tran, a senior lecturer in the University of Miami College of Arts and Sciences' Department of Classics, analyzed the classical text and applied her perspective as a blue and green humanist to amplify understanding of the Sirens' role in the story and its relationship to ancient Greco-Roman society.

"I'm like a detective going back to the source to see what the text actually says, which is also why you want to learn Greek or Roman for yourself—to know what it says in the original language," said Tran, who has written not only about the Sirens but also about other ancient sea creatures. "When you read the epic itself, it has little to do with how people, tradition and centuries have portrayed them."

To start, Tran noted that Homer offers no description of the Sirens' appearance.

"We have no idea what they look like. We don't even know if they have a body, and of course we don't hear their song," Tran pointed out. "Them not having a body and us not hearing the song correlate—a mystery dangled before our eyes, but we never get to the thing itself."

Homer tells us only that the Sirens live on an island, a rock, and sit in a green field, a meadow surrounded by heaps of dead men's bones, Tran noted, highlighting the juxtaposed imagery.

"In Greek myths, women, young girls—whether you're talking about Persephone or Medusa—often get raped in fields of blooming flowers. Yet here it's the inverse: The Sirens are sitting in the middle of this field surrounded by bones—all men's bones," Tran said. "And the description that the flesh is still rotting suggests recently dead, evoking the fact that danger is ever-present."

From Tran's perspective, this inversion is a nightmare scenario for these Greek males.

"This is women in control, and every time in Greek myths when you have women on their own, not part of the family structure, it's always the same story: They become a threat," said Tran. "Homer is not spelling it out for you, but essentially that's what he's saying. And we have stories in Greek myth of both boys and girls who choose not to marry, and terrible things happen to them."

title.en: How chromosomes find their partners
title.zh: 染色体如何寻找伴侣

summary.en: For a long time, so-called satellite DNA was considered largely worthless. Now, ETH Zurich researchers have shown in fruit flies that these repetitive sections of genetic material act as a kind of barcode, enabling the correct chromosomes to recognize one another.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

For a long time, so-called satellite DNA was considered largely worthless. Now, ETH Zurich researchers have shown in fruit flies that these repetitive sections of genetic material act as a kind of barcode, enabling the correct chromosomes to recognize one another.

The body cells of humans and animals contain a double set of chromosomes. One-half of the genetic material comes from the mother; the other stems from the father.

During the formation of sperm or egg cells, this double set of chromosomes must be halved to form a single set. This takes place during what is known as meiosis. In this process, a cell with a double set of chromosomes gives rise to daughter cells with a single set of chromosomes. This halving is necessary because, during fertilization, two germ cells—and thus their genetic material—fuse together.

Afterwards, there is once again a double set of chromosomes. If this did not happen, the number of chromosomes would double from one generation to the next as the germ cells fuse.

To ensure that chromosomes can be distributed evenly during meiosis, the maternal and paternal versions of the same chromosome must locate one another within a cell and temporarily pair up. This is no easy task amid the vast jumble of the cell nucleus. Mismatches must be avoided at all costs during the pairing phase to prevent chromosomes from being distributed incorrectly.

But how do the matching chromosome pairs actually find each other? ETH researchers led by Madhav Jagannathan, a professor at the Department of Biochemistry, and his Ph.D. student Lena Skrutl have now investigated—using the example of egg cell formation in female fruit flies (Drosophila)—how this "matchmaking" process takes place in the cell nucleus and have made a surprising discovery.

For a long time, scientists have known that large swaths of animal genomes consist of repetitive DNA sequences. Known as satellite DNA, experts regarded these repeats as useless "junk DNA" because they do not contain blueprints for proteins. Nor were other researchers able to attribute any role to satellite DNA during meiosis. Indeed, when they removed these satellite DNA repeats from just one chromosome, chromosome pairing still proceeded without error.

In Nature Communications , researchers from ETH demonstrate that unique satellite DNA patterns on each pair of chromosomes, comparable to a barcode on a product in a supermarket, help matching chromosomes find each other.

body.en: Common medications may reshape the gut microbiome long after the last dose is taken. In a study of more than 2,500 people, researchers found lasting microbial changes linked not only to antibiotics, but also to antidepressants, beta-blockers, acid-reducing drugs, and benzodiazepines. Some effects were still detectable years later, suggesting past medication use may strongly influence the gut bacteria people carry today.

summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Backyard bird feeding is one of our country’s most popular pastimes. Research reveals about half of Australian households feed wild birds, with many people doing so daily.

However, this practice could act as a superspreader event – where a disease infects an unusually high number of people or animals – of the H5N1 virus. This deadly strain of bird flu has already decimated wild bird and mammal populations worldwide. It is now spreading across Australia, most recently killing more than 1,000 crested terns and a long-nosed fur seal, the first detection in a mainland mammal.

Although many Australians feed wild birds, the practice is controversial . This is mainly due to concerns about people offering unsuitable foods and birds becoming dependent on humans.

So why is backyard bird feeding such a problem when it comes to bird flu? And can we do it safely?

People feed wild birds for various reasons , including to provide food during tough times or simply enjoy their presence. Most care deeply about their avian companions and believe feeding them is helpful .

Feeding wild birds heightens the risk of disease transmission at feeding locations . When we offer supplementary food, such as seeds or meat scraps, this attracts birds of many different species in a combination and number that would not happen in nature. They may carry deadly diseases, such as the H5N1 virus, and potentially spread them to other birds.

This can create a transmission hotspot right on our back deck. And catching bird flu can push our most threatened species, such as the orange-bellied parrot , to the brink of extinction.

The fatal effects of H5N1 are not only contained to birds. Scavenger animals such as possums, red foxes and crows can be exposed to the virus while devouring the carcasses of infected birds. Humans in close contact with infected wildlife, such as wildlife carers and veterinarians, can contract H5N1. However, human infection is rare and typically only causes mild symptoms.

Backyard bird feeding may seem like a harmless hobby. But given how many people do it, and the risks it poses to both birds and people, bird feeding activities could lead to many more wildlife deaths .

The most effective strategy is to stop feeding birds altogether. If you don’t offer food to wild birds, they will be less likely to congregate in your backyard or garden. And they will be fine without your help. Our previous research found most birds that visit feeders obtain most of their nutrition from natural sources, such as insects and worms. So the food we provide is a snack, not an essential meal.

body.zh: 后院喂鸟是我国最受欢迎的消遣之一。研究显示，大约一半的澳大利亚家庭喂养野生鸟类，其中许多人每天都这样做。 然而，这种做法可能会成为 H5N1 病毒的超级传播事件——一种疾病感染异常多的人或动物。这种致命的禽流感病毒已经导致世界各地的野生鸟类和哺乳动物数量大量减少。它目前正在澳大利亚各地蔓延，最近导致 1,000 多只凤头燕鸥和一只长鼻海豹死亡，这是首次在大陆哺乳动物中发现这种病毒。 尽管许多澳大利亚人喂养野生鸟类，但这种做法存在争议。这主要是由于担心人们提供不合适的食物以及鸟类变得依赖人类。 那么，为什么在禽流感方面，后院喂鸟会成为一个问题呢？我们可以安全地做到这一点吗？ 人们出于各种原因喂养野生鸟类，包括在困难时期提供食物或只是享受它们的存在。大多数人非常关心他们的鸟类同伴，并相信喂养它们是有帮助的。 喂养野鸟会增加喂养地点疾病传播的风险。当我们提供补充食物（例如种子或肉末）时，会吸引许多不同物种的鸟类，其组合和数量在自然界中是不会发生的。它们可能携带致命疾病，例如 H5N1 病毒，并有可能将其传播给其他鸟类。 这可以在我们的后甲板上创建一个传输热点。感染禽流感可能会将橙腹鹦鹉等最受威胁的物种推向灭绝的边缘。 H5N1 的致命影响不仅限于鸟类。负鼠、红狐和乌鸦等食腐动物在吞食受感染鸟类的尸体时可能会接触到病毒。与受感染野生动物密切接触的人类，例如野生动物护理人员和兽医，可能会感染 H5N1。然而，人类感染很少见，通常只会引起轻微症状。 后院喂鸟似乎是一种无害的爱好。但考虑到有多少人这样做，以及它对鸟类和人类造成的风险，鸟类喂养活动可能会导致更多野生动物死亡。 最有效的策略是完全停止喂养鸟类。如果您不向野鸟提供食物，它们就不太可能聚集在您的后院或花园里。没有你的帮助，他们也会没事的。我们之前的研究发现，大多数访问喂食器的鸟类从昆虫和蠕虫等天然来源获取大部分营养。所以我们提供的食物是零食，而不是必需的膳食。 装满种子和剩余肉的喂食器会吸引更多的鸟类。因此，为了阻止他们聚集，只需提供更少的食物即可。就像新冠病毒时代的社交......

title.en: UK's rarest bird of prey rears new chicks in secret location
title.zh: 英国最稀有的猛禽在秘密地点抚养新雏鸟

summary.en: The Montagu Harrier successfully nested for the second year running in the same secret location.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The UK's rarest bird of prey has successfully nested for the second year running in the same secret location, the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) has reported.

A male Montagu's harrier, known as "AU" by conservationists, bred with two different females, rearing six chicks across two nests on English farmland.

Montagu's harriers were put on a "red list" of birds most at risk in the UK in 2021. Numbers have declined from a high of nine successful nests in 2011, to no evidence of successful breeding between 2020 and 2024.

An RSPB spokesperson said: "We are doing our absolute utmost to save this iconic species in the UK and are delighted with six flying juveniles this year."

The charity said careful monitoring, in partnership with the farmers on whose land the birds nested, meant the nests were protected by fences to exclude ground predators such as foxes.

The single male Montagu's harrier has also been working very hard to keep his two nests of hungry chicks fed.

The BBC was given exclusive access to the nest and was able to witness some of the spectacular feeding behaviour of the raptors: the male drops prey in mid-air and the female rolls upside down to catch it in her talons.

These slender, long-winged raptors make an epic annual migration to Africa in winter and return to Europe to nest over summer, often setting up home in agricultural fields.

But little is known about the behaviour of juvenile harriers once they leave the nest. This year, for the first time, the RSPB has fitted two of the chicks with satellite tags in the hope of providing the birds with better protection.

"It will allow us for the first time ever to work out where they're going, what migration route, how long they'll spend there, and will they come back to the UK in the first year or the second year," said Mark Thomas, head of investigations at the RSPB.

It is also hoped the tagging can better protect the rare birds from having their nests, on the ground, hidden among crops, inadvertently destroyed.

"This is a species right on the brink, and climate change is not helping that. The harvest here, for example, this year, was like a month earlier than in previous years. So it almost puts any Montagu's harrier nest at the peril of inadvertently being destroyed by farm machinery," said Thomas.

Conservationists have urged birders to look out for the youngsters, and report any sightings by emailing the RSPB's Montagu's hotline at montys@rspb.org.uk.
body.zh: 据英国皇家鸟类保护协会 (RSPB) 报道，英国最稀有的猛禽已连续第二年在同一秘密地点成功筑巢。 一只雄性蒙塔古鹞被自然资源保护者称为“AU”，与两只不同的雌性一起繁殖，在英国农田的两个巢中养育了六只雏鸟。 2021 年，蒙塔古鹞被列入英国最危险鸟类的“红色名单”。数量已从 2011 年成功筑巢 9 个的高峰下降到 2020 年至 2024 年间没有成功繁殖的证据。 皇家鸟类保护协会的一位发言人表示：“我们正在尽最大努力拯救英国的这一标志性物种，我们对今年有六只飞行幼崽感到高兴。” 该慈善机构表示，与鸟儿筑巢的土地上的农民合作进行仔细监控，意味着鸟巢受到栅栏的保护，以排除狐狸等地面掠食者。 单身雄性蒙塔古鹞也一直在非常努力地工作，以保证他的两窝饥饿的雏鸟有吃的。 英国广播公司获得了进入猛禽巢穴的独家访问权限，并目睹了猛禽的一些壮观的进食行为：雄性猛禽将猎物抛在半空中，雌性则翻滚着用爪子捕捉猎物。 这些细长、长翼的猛禽每年冬天都会进行一次史诗般的迁徙，前往非洲，并在夏天返回欧洲筑巢，通常在农田里安家。 但人们对幼年鹞离开巢穴后的行为知之甚少。今年，皇家鸟类保护协会首次为其中两只小鸟安装了卫星标签，希望为这些小鸟提供更好的保护。 英国皇家鸟类保护协会调查负责人马克·托马斯表示：“这将使我们有史以来第一次弄清楚他们要去哪里、迁徙路线是什么、他们将在那里待多久，以及他们会在第一年还是第二年回到英国。” 人们还希望标签能够更好地保护这些稀有鸟类的巢穴，它们在地面上、隐藏在农作物中的巢穴不会被无意中破坏。 “这是一个濒临灭绝的物种，气候变化对此无济于事。例如，今年这里的收成比往年早了一个月。因此，这几乎使任何蒙塔古鹞巢都面临着被农业机械无意中摧毁的危险，”托马斯说。 环保人士敦促观鸟者留意这些幼鸟，并通过电子邮件报告皇家鸟类保护协会蒙塔古热线：montys@rspb.org.uk。

body.en: 27 August 1926 : Air-pilots report seeing wasps and small green flies almost a mile-high in the sky The report by experienced air-pilots of a wasp at 6,000 feet and small green flies – probably aphides – at 4,000 should make us realise how little we know of the habits of the common creatures which we, boastfully, think we understand. Who would imagine that a wasp could ascend so high! It has proved that it can, but what did it go up for? A certain town-tip that I pass occasionally is a great place for wasps; they swarm over the rags, paper, tins, and rubbish of all kinds, and undoubtedly find much that for their grubs is fattening food in what man has thrown away as useless. Probably the old meat and fruit tins, jam pots too, are mines of treasure for these busy wasps. But surely no wasp expects to find a town-tip up in the sky, nor can it be worth the labour of ascent to that altitude in the hope of finding winged game, though the wasp is an excellent fly-catcher. The mother or queen wasps are busy laying eggs, so that cannot have tempted a drone to seek a mate in the upper air. Nuptial flight may explain the swarm of green flies at a great height; many insects ascend when they are stirred by amorous impulse, and high flight must influence distribution. A strong wind would carry them far from their original home, and doubtless many insect hordes are swept out to sea and trouble us no more. Continue reading...
body.zh: 1926 年 8 月 27 日：飞行员报告称在几乎一英里高的天空中看到了黄蜂和小绿蝇。经验丰富的飞行员报告称在 6,000 英尺高空发现了黄蜂，在 4,000 英尺高处发现了小绿蝇（可能是蚜虫），这应该让我们意识到，我们对这些我们自以为了解的常见生物的习性知之甚少。谁能想到黄蜂能飞得这么高！事实证明可以，但是它涨起来是为了什么？我偶尔经过的某个城镇尖端是黄蜂的好地方。它们成群结队地爬过破布、纸张、罐头盒和各种垃圾，毫无疑问，它们在人类丢弃的无用物品中发现了许多让它们的幼虫增肥的食物。对于这些忙碌的黄蜂来说，旧的肉类和水果罐头、果酱罐可能都是宝藏。但毫无疑问，没有黄蜂期望在天空中找到城镇的顶端，也不值得为了寻找有翅膀的猎物而费力爬到那个高度，尽管黄蜂是出色的捕蝇者。黄蜂妈妈或蜂王正忙于产卵，因此不可能诱使雄蜂在高空寻找配偶。婚飞也许可以解释为什么绿蝇会飞到很高的地方。许多昆虫在受到爱情冲动的刺激时就会上升，高飞必然会影响分布。一阵强风会将它们吹离原来的家园，毫无疑问，许多昆虫群会被卷入大海，不再打扰我们。继续阅读...
